summary: Lighthouse on a wooded island in western Lake Erie, off Put-in-Bay: first tower burned in 1863-64, limestone rebuild, lit from a steel skeleton tower since 1939.

structures.note: First light; burned on the night of 31 December 1863 or 1 January 1864 (sources differ)
Two-story limestone keeper's house with a square tower; the ruin stands today
Active light. Light List gives focal height 80 ft (24.4 m); Gora gives the tower as 67 ft (20.5 m)

access.note: State wildlife refuge; entry is unlawful without authorization from the chief of the Division of Wildlife or their designee (Ohio Admin. Code 1501:31-15-07). The USLHS place record says Open to Public: No.

facts.agency: Ohio Division of Wildlife (state wildlife refuge); property transferred to the State of Ohio in 1961

events.note: Congress's $5,000 appropriation for a light on Green Island (the 1864 newspaper gives 1851); site bought from Alfred P. Edwards for $500 in December 1851 (LighthouseFriends)
Brick light tower and keeper's dwelling; LighthouseFriends says the contractor finished in late November 1854
Fourth-order revolving lens, per LighthouseFriends. The Register instead describes a French mirror
Not exhibited until 1855: defect in the revolving machinery and the lateness of the season (LighthouseFriends)

First light burned on the night of 31 December 1863 or 1 January 1864. The 5 January 1864 newspaper says Friday evening last (read literally, Friday 1 January). Thorndale (1898) places the fire on the outgoing of 1863 and incoming of 1864; LighthouseFriends says New Year's Day 1864.
Two-story limestone light with square tower, in service 1 July 1865 (LighthouseFriends); Gora says built by July 1865
Changed to fixed white varied by a red flash every minute (LighthouseFriends date)
Boathouse built on the east end of the island, with boatways and an iron winch (LighthouseFriends)
Landing superstructure damaged by ice during the winter before the 1892 report (running head 1892; volume labelled 1891-92), then repaired and reballasted
Wharf extended 30 feet and made 16 feet wide for the light-house tender
Carriage and iron track provided to take the keeper's large boat from the water (report running head 1896; volume labelled 1896-97; Tenth District)
From fixed white varied by a red flash every minute to flashing alternately red and white with thirty-second intervals (Light-House Board, change effective 1 April 1901)
Keeper William L. Gordon towed a disabled launch with two men and two women aboard to Put in Bay on 25 July 1919
Sheds removed; inclosed veranda and cistern built, $1,030 (fiscal 1921)
Superstructure of the wharf rebuilt, $1,843 (fiscal 1922)
Light automated; Keeper Gordon transferred to South Bass Island Light (LighthouseFriends)
Coast Guard automated light on an eighty-foot steel skeletal tower about 960 feet southwest of the old light (LighthouseFriends); Gora describes a 67 ft (20.5 m) steel skeletal tower
Old light discontinued
Lighthouse property transferred from the federal government to the State of Ohio (LighthouseFriends)
April 1974: two fishermen landed and started a fire that raged for a full day, leaving only a shell of the old limestone lighthouse (LighthouseFriends).
National Register of Historic Places, as part of the Light Stations of Ohio multiple-property listing

corrections.why: The 2025 Light List lists Green Island Light (LLNR 5535) as lit on a skeleton tower, and Gora says that light is still in service. The old 1864-65 light has been inactive since 1939, so the editor may want the station to read active with the old light noted.

corrections.proposed: tower built 1865, standing as a ruin; steel skeletal tower built 1939, active
corrections.why: The first tower (begun 1854, lit 1855) burned in 1863 or 1864. The standing ruin is the limestone light of 1864-65, and the active light is on a 1939 steel tower that the record omits.
Light List 2025 position for LLNR 5535 (41-38-42.140N, 082-52-04.265W), the active light. The OSM point used now is about 72 m away. For a human to confirm.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1864 newspaper and USLHS give 1854. LighthouseFriends says the tower was finished in late November 1854 but not shown until 1855 because of a machinery defect and the late season; Rowlett and Wikidata give 1855. The story says built 1854 and first shown 1855.

The 5 January 1864 newspaper says the light burned on Friday evening last, which read literally is Friday 1 January 1864. Thorndale (1898) places the fire on the outgoing of 1863 and the incoming of 1864 (31 December 1863 into 1 January). LighthouseFriends says New Year's Day 1864. The story gives 1863 and states the disagreement.
The newspaper calls the 1854 light a flash light with a costly French mirror; LighthouseFriends describes a fourth-order revolving lens. Both are in the story and neither is settled.

resolved_conflicts.field: keepers: George F. Ferguson transfer to Green Island
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Ryall's 1913 story says Ferguson had held the Green Island post 'since June, 1905', which matches LighthouseFriends and the roster (1905). Her 'two years' at Lorain, counted from the 1902 promotion, would end about 1904. The story uses June 1905 and states the arithmetic.

Thorndale (1898): Green Island 'two miles distant'; LighthouseFriends: 'three miles southwest of Put-in-Bay'; Bigsby's 1822 letter (reprinted by Gora): 'Four miles from Put-in-Bay harbour'. Not settled. The story states all three.
LighthouseFriends says Delafield, visiting in October 1820, discovered the celestite. Gora says his topographer Louis de Russy found it in 1819. The story states both.
LighthouseFriends: one of twenty-one small islands in the Erie Archipelago. Gora: one of fourteen islands in Ohio's Bass Islands archipelago. Not reconciled; the story states both.

LighthouseFriends attributes the 1901 newspaper story of Italian greyhounds to keeper John Safe (1899-1903). Gora places the team with the keeper who came after Ferguson, which would put it after 1914. The newspaper was not read. The story states both.

notes_for_editor: Same-name trap: the Bulletin 1912-17 and 1918-23 indexes, the Commissioner's fiscal 1915 and 1921 keeper lists and the Bulletin 1914 all name Frank A. and George W. Drew at Green Island Light Station, Wis. (Green Bay), not Ohio. I did not attribute them to this station. Gordon's name is variously William L./G./J. in the Bulletin index; the 1922 letter and the roster say William L. The index's Gordon rescue at p. 91 could not be located in the text, so it is not used. The 1901 greyhound story is LighthouseFriends' attribution to John Safe; Gora's text places greyhounds with Ferguson's successor, which conflicts; the story follows LighthouseFriends and says the newspaper was not read. The Ryall 1913 story and the Thorndale 1898 narrative are read only through Gora's 2020 reproduction (copyrighted compilation; the story paraphrases and quotes only short phrases from the public-domain originals). The USLHS roster is matched to this station by name only (USLHS gives no position); roster lines carry person slugs from roster.py. Light-House Board entries (1891-92, 1894, 1896-97, 1901) are read from OCR; scan pages are cited, printed page numbers unconfirmed; check the page images before print. The Commissioner keeper list (scan 558) and appropriation lists (scan 660, 748) are OCR. NPGallery metadata names 'Graham,T.N.' as architect; the NRHP nomination PDF is a not-digitised placeholder, so the architect is not used. Station record says inactive; Light List 2025 says active. Light List range 8 nm vs record 7.0 (ENC). USLHS place coordinates '41 64.55' are invalid (coord_suspect) and are not used. Mary V. Drake and Maria M. Van Epp are roster first assistants; the sources read do not say how they were related to the principal keepers. Visit access: the Ohio rule makes entry unlawful without authorization, so the story says so; ODNR's own page was not reachable (404). The NRHP nomination for NRIS 90001909 is not digitised (NPGallery PDF is a 22 KB placeholder); only the NPGallery metadata was used (listing 18 December 1990; the 'Light Stations of Ohio MPS' multiple listing). Wikipedia's Green Island Light article was read for leads only and is not cited. Gora's 2020 history and LighthouseFriends are copyrighted; the story paraphrases them and quotes only public-domain originals (the 1864 Register, Thorndale 1898, the Light-House Board reports, Bulletins and Commissioner reports) or short fragments. The Light List gives the active light 41-38-42.140N 082-52-04.265W, 72 m from the OSM point; the record location was not changed. Correction made on the second pass: LighthouseFriends says the fire was on New Year's Day 1864 (earlier draft wrongly said New Year's Eve for LighthouseFriends). The Gordon letter's signature reads 'L. GORDON, Keeper' in the 1922 Bulletin OCR; the story calls him the keeper and does not spell out his first name from the letter. The Bulletin OCR is poor in places: the quoted phrase 'we bear concerts, speeches, and the news' is quoted exactly as OCR'd. NRHP wording: NPGallery gives 'Date Published 12/18/1990'; the story reads it as the record date, not as a listing date. Ryall's 'lights used at night' is quoted from Gora's reprint. Mrs. K'Burg's remark is from Gora's 2004/2020 text and is paraphrased in the story (Gora is copyrighted; the story quotes no sentence of it). Fact-check 2026-10-22 (second reader): the story now states the three distances (Thorndale two miles; LighthouseFriends three miles southwest; Bigsby four miles via Gora) and the 14 against 21 island counts; the Delafield celestite credit (LighthouseFriends) is set against Gora's 1819 discovery by de Russy; the greyhound conflict is stated. Ryall's excerpt in Gora says Ferguson had been keeper at Green Island 'since June, 1905'. The earlier about-1904 reading was an arithmetic inference from her two years at Lorain and is now stated as such. Light-House Board report years are taken from the running heads: landing 1892, wharf 1894, carriage 1896 (Tenth District; the stairs and ruby-glass entry sits in the 1897 report), characteristic 1901 (Tenth District); scan pages were checked with corpus.py page. Bulletin 1922 letter: PDF p. 22 (printed p. 230); the old #page=230 pointed past the end of the 49-page PDF. Gordon's fiscal-1920 entry is a row of the 'Saving of Life and Property' table (scan 558, printed p. 60) matched by OCR column block: the name is one OCR line, but the act beside it does not line up in the text, so the story describes no act and the page image was not confirmed. The roster's provenance (NARA registers via Kraig Anderson) is the roster tool's own note and is not on the USLHS page, so the story no longer attributes it. Gora's 1939 tower is 67 ft (20.5 m) with an 80 ft focal plane; LighthouseFriends calls the tower eighty feet.
